item.title: Sen. Chris Van Hollen challenges Sen. Chuck Schumer to lead Democratic majority in next Congress
item.description: Schumer (New York) has led Senate Democrats for the past decade and never before faced a challenger. If Van Hollen (Maryland) is successful in his uphill bid, he would preside over a majority of at least 55 members that could stymie President Donald Trump’s agenda during his final two years in the White House. “The voters called for big change, and this is a time that we have to deliver for people across the country,” Van Hollen said about his decision.

item.title: Welcome to ‘The Vow,’ the dating show for budding tradwives. It’s really something, columnist Monica Hesse writes.
item.description: Earlier this year, the nation was experiencing what appeared to be a deeply felt interest in returning us to the (18)50s. And then the midterms happened. So “The Vow” — Fox Nation’s new dating reality show for people seeking “traditional” marriage — has arrived at an odd time.

item.title: Just after he shot five people, D.C. gunman said he had ‘to do something’ to draw attention to his condo dispute
item.description: Matt Lambert told a building manager after he shot five people in Washington, D.C., that he was tired of the mold and water damage in his unit. In 2025, Lambert filed a lawsuit against the condo association and property management company.

item.title: Police identify deceased victim in Logan Circle shooting as a manager at the condo building where the gunman lived
item.description: Authorities said James Stuart, 46, was shot with a handgun at a Vida Fitness gym near 15th and P streets NW.

item.title: Man who shot 5 in D.C. was a doctor who lived nearby, officials said, and had long-running dispute with condo building’s management
item.description: The attacker who opened fire in the Logan Circle neighborhood Thursday morning, killing one person and wounding four others, has been identified as Matt Lambert, a 55-year-old doctor, according to two officials. Records show that Lambert had filed a lawsuit alleging that his building’s condo association failed to act on his complaints about a mold problem and water damage inside his unit.

item.title: Hegseth awards a medal to soldier who admonished him and his team for talking loudly, laughing at Tomb of the Unknowns
item.description: A video of the incident, which followed a Veterans Day observance, elicited furious backlash from critics incredulous that a defense secretary would behave disrespectfully at one of the nation’s most sacred memorials.

item.title: Trump says no deal needed with Iran, closes down Vance negotiations
item.description: Vice President JD Vance in recent days had started outreach to hard-liners in Tehran to explore the possibility of a negotiated end to the conflict. The war — and the jump in gas and food prices that has come with it — is deeply unpopular among U.S. voters, who delivered a historic defeat to Republicans in the midterm elections last week.

item.title: Witnesses describe early moments of shooting on Logan Circle corner
item.description: Some fled a Vida gym after gunfire erupted, barricading themselves in a basement. Others tried to help a bleeding woman crumpled on the curb. One person was killed and four were injured in the shooting Thursday morning; police said the attacker was dead of an apparently self-inflicted gunshot wound after barricading themselves in an apartment.

item.title: 1 person killed, 4 injured in shooting that began in D.C. gym; suspect shot himself, police say
item.description: Interim D.C. police chief Jeffery Carroll said the gunman opened fire at a Vida Fitness gym near the intersection of 15th and P streets NW. The suspected attacker later barricaded himself inside a nearby apartment building, Carroll said, then shot himself after speaking to police for more than an hour.

item.description: William Howard Taft avoided foreign wars and worked to reduce tariffs. His presidency was “humdrum.”

item.description: Police were “working an active barricade” near the shooting, which occurred near the intersection of 15th and P streets NW, according to a department spokesperson.

item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after affair with alleged spy

item.description: D.C. police were searching for a suspect Thursday morning. A police spokesperson said the shooting happened at the intersection of 15th and P streets Northwest.

item.description: Among those injured in the three-story building collapse in Brooklyn on Wednesday were three firefighters, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday.

item.title: Nvidia board will meet to weigh fate of CEO Jensen Huang after his affair with alleged spy
item.description: Nvidia’s board is expected to meet late Wednesday, according to two people familiar with the matter, days after Huang admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia stock fell in after-hours trading following news reports of the board’s meeting and a second alleged affair by Huang with an Nvidia executive who reported to him.

item.title: Kennedy family sues to stop Trump’s triumphal arch, saying it will cast a shadow on John F. Kennedy’s gravesite
item.description: Nine members of the Kennedy family have sued the Trump administration to block the planned 250-foot-tall structure, which they said would “damage historically significant sightlines to the existing gravesites and memorials” at Arlington National Cemetery. A Post analysis found that the arch would briefly cover Kennedy’s memorial on 50 days of the year and his eternal flame on 18 days, while touching burial sites across the cemetery on 284 days over the year.

item.title: Hegseth escapes impeachment threat as House Republicans unite to prevent a vote
item.description: The result follows a coordinated effort within the Trump administration, including by the president, to defend the defense secretary. Hegseth held a rare Pentagon news conference Tuesday, during which he appealed directly to the president and his allies in Congress. The attempt to remove him from office had been led by Rep. Thomas Massie, a fellow Republican and frequent critic of President Donald Trump.

item.title: Supreme Court grapples with arguments over the power of federal agencies to impose fines
item.description: The case comes as the high court’s conservative majority has pared back the power of federal regulators in a series of recent cases. But even some conservatives appeared skeptical on Tuesday of going further.

item.title: At least 19 ICE recruits named in DHS hack were hired despite red flags, including past criminal charges or misconduct allegations
item.description: The Trump administration has onboarded thousands of new officers in an accelerated recruitment effort that has bypassed traditional background checks. The Post performed background checks on about 300 of those new hires after activists in October hacked a DHS employee database and released information about thousands of workers.
